_comment: Local Omarchy layer: Kioku (記憶, 'memory'), the name this family's archive goes by. local-build.sh applies it to its build copy after Noodle's apply-branding.sh (apply-kioku.sh), unless GALLERY_BRAND=noodle; verify-kioku.sh lists what still names Noodle Gallery, Gallery or Immich. README.md says what changes, what cannot, and how to classify a new string. The words below are read by both scripts: a name, title or alt here goes into code, so it holds no quotes, backticks, $, <, >, braces or backslashes.
name: Kioku

memory_player._comment: The shared memory player's tab: page_title until a memory has loaded, then memory_title, {title} being the memory's own.

manifest._comment: The installed app's splash ground, the theme's paper. No theme_color: the pages' own theme-color meta follows light and dark, and a fixed one would paint a dark window's bar white.

phone_app_icon._comment: The open-in-app banner offers the phone app, which stays Noodle Gallery's, beside an icon. apple-icon-180.png becomes the Kioku web app's own (assets), so the banner shows the phone app's icon instead, made from Noodle's iOS launcher icon.

about_credit._comment: Help › About, for the owner (the section only the admin sees, with the projects' links): the AGPL credit to the software Kioku runs on. Added to the bundle as its own key, in the ten maintained languages; the others fall back to English.

assets._comment: Each file in branding/kioku/assets/ replaces its counterparts in the build copy's web/static; a counterpart that is gone fails the build (upstream moved it). A file not drawn yet is a warning and Noodle's stays. Raster outputs are resized from the source; later entries overwrite earlier ones, so a hand-drawn small favicon beats the resized one. An optional source says what is made instead while it is not drawn: favicon.ico, for one, is assembled from the 16, 32 and 48 px PNGs.

the 48 px cut, drawn for its pixels
the 32 px cut, drawn for its pixels
the 16 px cut, drawn for its pixels

files.optional: assembled from the 16, 32 and 48 px PNGs

files.why: the installed app's icon: opaque, 1024 px, the mark inside the middle 80% (maskable)
the home-screen icon on an iPhone
the link preview for a shared link without a photo of its own (1200 × 630); the server's own share tags point at it too
the mark: the login backdrop, the bar on a narrow screen, every icon-sized logo (light)
the mark on a dark theme
the mark while a page loads, and the login card's logo (light)
the loader on a dark theme

the inline logo on a dark theme
the stacked logo on a dark theme

_comment: Every string in the folded bundle (i18n/*.json after apply-branding.sh) that names a brand is listed here exactly once, and apply-kioku.sh stops the build on one that is not: a new upstream or overlay string is classified by a person, never guessed. It also stops on a listed key that no longer exists or no longer names a brand, so a rule cannot go quiet after a rebase.

kioku: the web experience, where the name means this archive, its pages, its library or its database. Noodle Gallery (noodle_gallery) or the bare word Gallery (gallery) becomes Kioku, in every locale. Bare Gallery is only ever the brand in these keys; as a common noun ('Hide gallery') it is never touched.

keep: where Noodle Gallery means something that stays Noodle's: the phone app, the server's releases and versions, the project's support and purchase pages, and credits. verify-kioku.sh lists them and passes them.
restore: apply-branding's lower-case rewrite also took the ~/immich directory for the brand in the Curator messages; the path is put back.

phrases: grammar the swap alone would break, applied first, each where it is listed: an article or a demonstrative that agreed with Gallery, a case ending glued to the name. A phrase without keys applies to every Kioku key of its locale. The ten maintained locales are reviewed; the others get the word swapped, with whatever endings apply-branding left.

noodle_gallery._why: this archive as the family and the owner use it in the browser: its pages, library, database, maintenance and look

gallery._why: the overlay's own strings, where the bare word Gallery is the archive's name

phone_app._why: the phone app's own screens (no web page shows these): the app on the phone is Noodle Gallery's, built and named by Noodle

phone_app_on_web._why: web pages about the phone app, which the family installs and finds under Noodle Gallery's name: the open-in-app banner, the app's download page and onboarding step, Obtainium

server_releases._why: the server software's releases and versions: Noodle Gallery publishes them, and the server image stays Noodle's

purchase._why: supporting and buying a licence for the project behind it

credits._why: credits and the project's own documentation and resources

identifiers._why: lower-case forms that are paths, not the brand, beside the hostnames and schemes apply-branding.sh shields (its UPSTREAM_IDENTIFIERS_JSON)

restore._why: the owner's Curator lives under ~/immich; apply-branding read the directory as the brand in nine locales

_comment: What verify-kioku.sh passes outside the i18n bundle's keep list, each with the text around it that makes it what it is (near: a regular expression the 160 characters on either side must match), so the same word anywhere else still fails.
surfaces are the source files a build copy's check reads (titles, the manifest, app.html, the memory player, and the files apply-kioku.sh rewrites); a build output is read whole.

keep.why: About › Server details lists the server's own version, Noodle Gallery's (ServerAboutModal)
Help › About: the upstream project's own link, for the owner (the AGPL credit)
the Obtainium link names the phone app as upstream did; the phone app is Noodle's to rename
@immich/ui's own Logo, which only a Modal given icon={true} draws, and no page does; it is installed in the image, out of a source rewrite's reach
a comment heading a theme's generated CSS, never shown
the server software's security contact, Noodle's
